          defer() {
            echo "::notice::$1"
            curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
              --data-urlencode "job=seo-geo-scan" --data-urlencode "deferred=$1" \
              "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
            exit 0
          }
          fail() {
            echo "::error::$1"
            curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
              --data-urlencode "job=seo-geo-scan" \
              --data-urlencode "fail=$1" \
              "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
            exit 1
          }
          if [ "$AGENT" = "codex" ]; then
            probe=$(curl -s --max-time 30 -o /tmp/probe.json -w "%{http_code}" https://api.openai.com/v1/responses \
              -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
              -d '{"model":"gpt-5-mini","input":"ok","max_output_tokens":16}') || probe=000
            err=$(jq -r '.error.code // empty' /tmp/probe.json 2>/dev/null)
            case "$probe:$err" in
              2*:*|429:rate_limit_exceeded)
                defer "Codex hit a rate limit this run - it clears by itself, so the job stays due and is retried automatically. Not a failure." ;;
              429:*|402:*)
                fail "your OpenAI account cannot run builds right now (OpenAI said: ${err:-quota exceeded}). This does not fix itself by retrying - add credit or raise the limit at platform.openai.com/settings/organization/billing." ;;
              401:*|403:*)
                fail "OpenAI rejected the OPENAI_API_KEY secret on this repo (HTTP $probe). The key was probably revoked or rotated - create a new one at platform.openai.com/api-keys and set it again with 'gh secret set OPENAI_API_KEY'." ;;
              *)
                fail "workflow failed - $RUN_URL" ;;
            esac
          fi
          fail "workflow failed - $RUN_URL"

      - name: Report outcome to the dashboard
        if: always() && steps.classify.outputs.reported != '1'
        env:
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          OUTCOME: ${{ job.status }}
        run: |
          if [ "$OUTCOME" = "success" ]; then
            curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
              --data-urlencode "job=seo-geo-scan" --data-urlencode "ok=1" \
              "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
          else
            curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
              --data-urlencode "job=seo-geo-scan" \
              --data-urlencode "fail=workflow failed - $RUN_URL" \
              "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
          fi

name: SEO setup

# DISPATCH-ONLY personalization run, fired by the DispatchSEO backend right
# after it installs this pipeline (cloud zero-touch onboarding), or by hand
# via workflow_dispatch. It is the same setup the self-host owner runs in a
# local Claude Code session: read the repo, find or scaffold the content
# home, write .dispatchseo/conventions.md, fill the site profile - then call
# mark_pipeline_installed, which the backend re-verifies server-side before
# stamping the project as installed. Safe to re-run: setup is idempotent and
# reconciles instead of duplicating.

on:
  repository_dispatch:
    types: [seo-setup]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: seo-setup
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  setup:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Real runs take 5-15 minutes on a first pass; past 30 is a hang.
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Which coding agent personalizes this project - resolved at RUN time from
      # the dashboard, never baked in at install time.
      #
      # Same rule as the pnpm pin in the builder workflows, for the same reason:
      # a decision left to whoever ran the install is a decision someone
      # eventually forgets, and the failure mode here is a setup run that calls
      # the wrong agent. Asking the backend means switching agent on the
      # dashboard takes effect on the next run with nothing to edit in this repo.
      #
      # The fallback matters as much as the happy path: a repo installed against
      # a backend that predates the `agent` field gets no value here, and must
      # keep behaving exactly as it did - which is Claude, because Claude was the
      # only option that ever existed before the field.
      - name: Resolve the coding agent
        id: agent
        env:
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
          CLAUDE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          agent=""
          code=$(curl -s -o /tmp/agent.json -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 30 \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
            {{BACKEND_URL}}/api/project-mode) || code=unreachable
          [ "$code" = "200" ] && agent=$(jq -r '.agent // empty' /tmp/agent.json 2>/dev/null)
          if [ -z "$agent" ] || [ "$agent" = "null" ]; then
            # No answer from the backend. Infer from which secret exists, and
            # tie-break to claude - see the note above.
            if [ -n "$OPENAI_API_KEY" ] && [ -z "$CLAUDE_TOKEN" ]; then agent=codex; else agent=claude; fi
            echo "Backend did not name an agent (HTTP $code) - inferred '$agent' from the secrets on this repo."
          fi
          # Fail here, in plain language, rather than letting the agent's own
          # action die minutes in on a cryptic validation error. The 2026-07-17
          # dogfood install burned four runs on exactly that.
          case "$agent" in
            claude)
              if [ -z "$CLAUDE_TOKEN" ]; then
                echo "::error::This project builds with Claude Code, but the CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN secret is missing or empty on this repo. Reconnect Claude Code from your DispatchSEO dashboard (Settings), or set one by hand: run 'claude setup-token', then pipe the token into 'gh secret set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN' without any whitespace."
                exit 1
              fi
              case "$CLAUDE_TOKEN" in
                sk-ant-oat*) : ;;
                *)
                  echo "::error::CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN does not look like a Claude Code OAuth token (expected it to start with sk-ant-oat). It was probably line-wrapped or the wrong text was pasted when it was saved. Reconnect Claude Code from your DispatchSEO dashboard to store a verified replacement."
                  exit 1 ;;
              esac ;;
            codex)
              if [ -z "$OPENAI_API_KEY" ]; then
                echo "::error::This project builds with Codex, but the OPENAI_API_KEY secret is missing or empty on this repo. Add it with 'gh secret set OPENAI_API_KEY', or rerun the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard."
                exit 1
              fi
              case "$OPENAI_API_KEY" in
                sk-*) : ;;
                *)
                  echo "::error::OPENAI_API_KEY does not look like an OpenAI key (expected it to start with sk-). It was probably line-wrapped or the wrong text was pasted when it was saved. Create a fresh key at platform.openai.com/api-keys and set it again."
                  exit 1 ;;
              esac ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::The dashboard reported an unknown agent '$agent'. This repo's workflows are older than that setting - re-run the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard to update them."
              exit 1 ;;
          esac
          echo "agent=$agent" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Building with: $agent"

      # Fail loudly if the seo-manager MCP is unreachable - setup without the
      # backend would "succeed" while personalizing nothing.
      - name: Preflight - seo-manager MCP reachable
        env:
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          url=$(node -e "console.log(require('./.github/mcp-ci.json').mcpServers['seo-manager'].url)")
          code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 30 -X POST "$url" \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
            -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":0,"method":"tools/list"}')
          if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
            echo "::error::seo-manager MCP at $url returned HTTP $code - fix the URL in .github/mcp-ci.json or the SEO_MCP_API_KEY secret"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "seo-manager MCP OK ($url)"

      # Codex reads its MCP servers from a config.toml inside its own home
      # directory. Two things here are easy to get wrong and both are silent:
      #
      # 1. The action does NOT honour an inbound CODEX_HOME env var - it takes a
      #    `codex-home` INPUT and sets the env itself. Writing a config to a
      #    hand-rolled $CODEX_HOME and hoping is a no-op, and the failure looks
      #    like an agent with no tools rather than an error.
      # 2. `sandbox: workspace-write` blocks network by default, which kills MCP
      #    over HTTP. The network_access line below is what makes the sandboxed
      #    posture usable at all.
      - name: Write Codex's MCP config
        if: steps.agent.outputs.agent == 'codex'
        env:
          DATAFORSEO_LOGIN: ${{ secrets.DATAFORSEO_LOGIN }}
          DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/codex-home"
          cp .github/mcp-codex.toml "$RUNNER_TEMP/codex-home/config.toml"
          cat >> "$RUNNER_TEMP/codex-home/config.toml" <<'TOML'

          [sandbox_workspace_write]
          network_access = true
          TOML
          # Render the DataForSEO credential tokens. Codex's TOML `env` map is
          # LITERAL - it does not expand ${VAR} the way Claude expands its JSON
          # config - so left alone the dataforseo server would authenticate as
          # the literal string "${DATAFORSEO_LOGIN}" and every keyword call
          # would 401 mid-build. python3 rather than sed so no credential
          # character can break the substitution; values are TOML-escaped. A
          # truncated config (free-mode project, no dataforseo section) makes
          # this a no-op.
          python3 - "$RUNNER_TEMP/codex-home/config.toml" <<'PY'
          import os, sys
          path = sys.argv[1]
          text = open(path).read()
          for token, var in (("${DATAFORSEO_LOGIN}", "DATAFORSEO_LOGIN"),
                             ("${DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD}", "DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD")):
              val = os.environ.get(var, "").replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"')
              text = text.replace(token, val)
          open(path, "w").write(text)
          PY
          echo "Codex home prepared. Servers configured:"
          grep -E '^\[mcp_servers\.' "$RUNNER_TEMP/codex-home/config.toml"

      - name: Run setup
        if: steps.agent.outputs.agent == 'claude'
        id: claude
        # Never fail the job at this step: the classify step below reads the
        # outcome and decides what the run MEANS (transient rate limit vs dead
        # account), which it can only do if it is reachable.
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
        with:
          # Cloud fires this as the DispatchSEO GitHub App (a Bot actor), and the App also authored the workflow commits, so scheduled runs are bot-actored too. Every trigger here needs repo write access, so allowing bots is safe; without this claude-code-action aborts with "non-human actor".
          allowed_bots: "*"
          claude_code_oauth_token: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # Full transcript in the step log - setup decisions (content home,
          # conventions) should stay auditable after the fact.
          show_full_output: true
          prompt: "FIRST call the seo-manager MCP tool get_instructions with workflow setup, then follow the returned markdown exactly - it is the current playbook and overrides any cached knowledge of this pipeline. In brief: study this repo and the live site, find or scaffold the content home, write .dispatchseo/conventions.md, fill the site profile via the seo-manager MCP, verify the pipeline prerequisites, and finish by calling mark_pipeline_installed. Commit any repo changes with git using the provided GITHUB_TOKEN, exactly as the instructions direct. Setup is idempotent - reconcile what exists, never duplicate. If get_instructions is unavailable, fail loudly and exit without changes."
          claude_args: |
            --mcp-config ./.github/mcp-ci.json
            --permission-mode bypassPermissions
            --max-turns 150
        env:
          CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
          DATAFORSEO_LOGIN: ${{ secrets.DATAFORSEO_LOGIN }}
          DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD }}
          MCP_TIMEOUT: "120000"

      # The Codex twin. Same prompt, verbatim - the agent's behaviour must not
      # depend on which one is holding the playbook, and the playbook itself
      # arrives from get_instructions either way.
      #
      # Model: gpt-5 by default, overridable with a repo variable because model
      # availability is per-account, not universal - `gpt-5-codex` 404s on a
      # pay-as-you-go project key even though it appears in GET /v1/models. Set
      # SEO_CODEX_MODEL in the repo's Actions variables to change it without
      # touching this file.
      #
      # There is NO turn budget to set. Codex has no --max-turns equivalent and
      # OpenAI closed the request for one as not-planned, so the job's
      # timeout-minutes above is the only ceiling on a runaway run.
      - name: Run setup (Codex)
        if: steps.agent.outputs.agent == 'codex'
        id: codex
        # Never fail the job at this step: the classify step below reads the
        # outcome and decides what the run MEANS (transient rate limit vs dead
        # account), which it can only do if it is reachable.
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: openai/codex-action@v1
        with:
          openai-api-key: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
          # Same rule as the Claude twin's allowed_bots above: cloud fires this
          # as the DispatchSEO GitHub App (a Bot actor) and scheduled runs are
          # bot-actored too, because the App authored the workflow commits.
          # codex-action's actor gate rejects EVERY bot by default (a bot 404s
          # the collaborator-permission lookup), so without this line each
          # unattended Codex run dies before Codex is even installed - while a
          # manual workflow_dispatch passes, which is what hides the failure.
          # Every trigger that can reach this step already required repo write
          # access, so allowing all actors adds nothing an attacker can use.
          allow-users: "*"
          model: ${{ vars.SEO_CODEX_MODEL || 'gpt-5' }}
          codex-home: ${{ runner.temp }}/codex-home
          sandbox: workspace-write
          # Strips sudo from the runner user for the rest of the job. Safe here:
          # everything after this step is curl. It is also more than the Claude
          # half of this pipeline does, which runs with bypassPermissions and no
          # sandbox at all.
          safety-strategy: drop-sudo
          output-file: ${{ runner.temp }}/codex-out.txt
          prompt: "ENVIRONMENT RULE (read first, it overrides habit): you have no apply_patch tool here - only the shell, and you are running UNATTENDED, so there is nobody to answer a question. Write every file with a SINGLE-QUOTED heredoc (cat > path <<'DSEOF' ... DSEOF) or with python3 reading the content from stdin. The quoted delimiter is the whole point: bash expands NOTHING inside it, so the backticks and $ in MDX and TSX survive verbatim. NEVER use an unquoted heredoc, printf or echo to write file content - an unquoted heredoc is what expands backticks and corrupts the file. Pick a delimiter that cannot appear in the content. Verify every write with ls -l and head before moving on, and never let a filename come from an unset shell variable. If you ever find yourself about to ask for approval or a go/no-go, do not: pick the safest option that still completes the task, do it, and say what you chose in the final report. A run that stops to ask a question builds nothing and is a failed run. FIRST call the seo-manager MCP tool get_instructions with workflow setup, then follow the returned markdown exactly - it is the current playbook and overrides any cached knowledge of this pipeline. In brief: study this repo and the live site, find or scaffold the content home, write .dispatchseo/conventions.md, fill the site profile via the seo-manager MCP, verify the pipeline prerequisites, and finish by calling mark_pipeline_installed. Commit any repo changes with git using the provided GITHUB_TOKEN, exactly as the instructions direct. Setup is idempotent - reconcile what exists, never duplicate. If get_instructions is unavailable, fail loudly and exit without changes."
        env:
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
          DATAFORSEO_LOGIN: ${{ secrets.DATAFORSEO_LOGIN }}
          DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD }}
          # This workflow's prompt names $GITHUB_TOKEN explicitly. Claude gets
          # it from the action's github_token: input; the Codex action has no
          # such input, so it has to be set here or the agent reads an empty
          # variable at the exact moment it tries to commit.
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # Phone the outcome home: failures land on the DispatchSEO dashboard
      # banner + alert email (same rails as the crons); successes clear any
      # earlier red banner row for this job.
      # A Codex failure is classified before it is reported. OpenAI's own
      # error.code distinguishes a transient per-minute rate limit (deferred -
      # the job stays due and the backend re-dispatches within hours) from an
      # account that cannot build (loud failure naming the billing fix). The
      # CLI's text cannot make that distinction - it collapses every 429 into
      # one message - so the probe asks the API directly. Without this step a
      # routine OpenAI rate limit was a red banner plus an alert email AND a
      # full cadence window lost, which on a weekly workflow is the week.
      # Claude failures keep their existing loud path.
      - name: Classify the outcome
        id: classify
        env:
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
          AGENT: ${{ steps.agent.outputs.agent }}
          AGENT_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.agent.outputs.agent == 'codex' && steps.codex.outcome || steps.claude.outcome }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          [ "$AGENT_OUTCOME" = "failure" ] || exit 0
          # From here this step owns the report; the flag stops the step below
          # writing a second (ok or generic-fail) row on top of this one.
          echo "reported=1" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          defer() {
            echo "::notice::$1"
            curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
              --data-urlencode "job=seo-setup" --data-urlencode "deferred=$1" \
              "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
            exit 0
          }
          fail() {
            echo "::error::$1"
            curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
              --data-urlencode "job=seo-setup" \
              --data-urlencode "fail=$1" \
              "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
            exit 1
          }
          if [ "$AGENT" = "codex" ]; then
            probe=$(curl -s --max-time 30 -o /tmp/probe.json -w "%{http_code}" https://api.openai.com/v1/responses \
              -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
              -d '{"model":"gpt-5-mini","input":"ok","max_output_tokens":16}') || probe=000
            err=$(jq -r '.error.code // empty' /tmp/probe.json 2>/dev/null)
            case "$probe:$err" in
              2*:*|429:rate_limit_exceeded)
                defer "Codex hit a rate limit this run - it clears by itself, so the job stays due and is retried automatically. Not a failure." ;;
              429:*|402:*)
                fail "your OpenAI account cannot run builds right now (OpenAI said: ${err:-quota exceeded}). This does not fix itself by retrying - add credit or raise the limit at platform.openai.com/settings/organization/billing." ;;
              401:*|403:*)
                fail "OpenAI rejected the OPENAI_API_KEY secret on this repo (HTTP $probe). The key was probably revoked or rotated - create a new one at platform.openai.com/api-keys and set it again with 'gh secret set OPENAI_API_KEY'." ;;
              *)
                fail "workflow failed - $RUN_URL" ;;
            esac
          fi
          fail "workflow failed - $RUN_URL"

      - name: Report outcome to the dashboard
        if: always() && steps.classify.outputs.reported != '1'
        env:
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          OUTCOME: ${{ job.status }}
        run: |
          if [ "$OUTCOME" = "success" ]; then
            curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
              --data-urlencode "job=seo-setup" --data-urlencode "ok=1" \
              "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
          else
            curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
              --data-urlencode "job=seo-setup" \
              --data-urlencode "fail=setup run failed - $RUN_URL" \
              "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
          fi

name: SEO health check

# Daily pre-flight, before the 05:13 builder: proves this project's coding-agent
# credential still works, and checks whether the installed pipeline is stale.
# Both outcomes phone home to the DispatchSEO dashboard (banner + email on
# failure), so a dead credential is a red alert at 04:18 - not a mystery failed
# build at 05:13.
#
# Cost: one tiny Claude call on the owner's own subscription, or - on Codex -
# roughly a hundredth of a cent, because that branch asks OpenAI about the key
# instead of spending a whole agent run to find out.

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "18 4 * * *" # 04:18 UTC daily, before the 05:13 builder (offset off the top of the hour)
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  health:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Which agent's credential to prove. Resolved at RUN time from the
      # dashboard, same as the builders - a health check that tests the wrong
      # credential is worse than none, because it reports green while the thing
      # that actually builds is dead.
      - name: Resolve the coding agent
        id: agent
        env:
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
          CLAUDE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          agent=""
          code=$(curl -s -o /tmp/agent.json -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 30 \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
            {{BACKEND_URL}}/api/project-mode) || code=unreachable
          [ "$code" = "200" ] && agent=$(jq -r '.agent // empty' /tmp/agent.json 2>/dev/null)
          if [ -z "$agent" ] || [ "$agent" = "null" ]; then
            if [ -n "$OPENAI_API_KEY" ] && [ -z "$CLAUDE_TOKEN" ]; then agent=codex; else agent=claude; fi
          fi
          case "$agent" in claude|codex) : ;; *) agent=claude ;; esac
          echo "agent=$agent" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Checking the $agent credential."

      # One minimal model call. If the token is dead/revoked/limited, this
      # step fails and the failure handler below reports the real reason.
      - name: Claude token liveness
        id: liveness
        if: steps.agent.outputs.agent == 'claude'
        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
        with:
          # Cloud fires this as the DispatchSEO GitHub App (a Bot actor), and the App also authored the workflow commits, so scheduled runs are bot-actored too. Every trigger here needs repo write access, so allowing bots is safe; without this claude-code-action aborts with "non-human actor".
          allowed_bots: "*"
          claude_code_oauth_token: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          prompt: "Reply with exactly: ok"
          claude_args: |
            --max-turns 1

      # Codex's liveness is a direct API call rather than a Codex run, and that
      # is deliberate. A Claude OAuth token can only be proven by using it, so
      # that branch spends a model call. An OpenAI key's health is a property
      # OpenAI will state outright - and its answer carries `error.code`, which
      # distinguishes "rate-limited for a minute" from "this account is out of
      # credit". Running the whole action here would cost more, take longer, and
      # tell us LESS, because the CLI collapses every 429 into one message.
      - name: Codex key liveness
        id: liveness_codex
        if: steps.agent.outputs.agent == 'codex'
        env:
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$OPENAI_API_KEY" ]; then
            echo "This project builds with Codex, but the OPENAI_API_KEY secret is missing or empty on this repo. Add it with 'gh secret set OPENAI_API_KEY', or re-run the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard." > "$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-failure.txt"
            cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-failure.txt"; exit 1
          fi
          code=$(curl -s --max-time 30 -o /tmp/live.json -w "%{http_code}" https://api.openai.com/v1/responses \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -d '{"model":"gpt-5-mini","input":"ok","max_output_tokens":16}') || code=000
          err=$(jq -r '.error.code // empty' /tmp/live.json 2>/dev/null)
          case "$code:$err" in
            2*:*) echo "OpenAI key is live." ; exit 0 ;;
            429:rate_limit_exceeded)
              # Transient by definition. A health check that goes red on a
              # momentary rate limit trains people to ignore the banner.
              echo "OpenAI is rate-limiting this key right now - that clears by itself, so treating it as healthy." ; exit 0 ;;
            429:*|402:*)
              echo "your OpenAI account cannot run builds (OpenAI said: ${err:-quota exceeded}). Retrying will not fix this - add credit or raise the limit at platform.openai.com/settings/organization/billing." > "$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-failure.txt" ;;
            401:*|403:*)
              echo "OpenAI rejected the OPENAI_API_KEY secret on this repo (HTTP $code). The key was probably revoked or rotated - create a new one at platform.openai.com/api-keys and set it again with 'gh secret set OPENAI_API_KEY'." > "$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-failure.txt" ;;
            *)
              echo "could not reach OpenAI to check the key (HTTP $code)." > "$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-failure.txt" ;;
          esac
          cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-failure.txt"; exit 1

      - name: Report token OK
        if: success()
        env:
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
            --data-urlencode "job=seo-token-check" --data-urlencode "ok=1" \
            "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true

      # Surface the real API error (revoked? usage limit?) and phone it home.
      # Full transcripts stay hidden - only the final result line is read.
      - name: Report token failure with the reason
        if: failure()
        env:
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
          AGENT: ${{ steps.agent.outputs.agent }}
        run: |
          reason="credential check failed (no error detail captured)"
          fix="re-run the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard"
          if [ "$AGENT" = "codex" ]; then
            # The Codex branch already resolved OpenAI's own error code into a
            # sentence naming the actual fix, so pass that through rather than
            # flattening it back into a generic message.
            msg=$(cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/agent-failure.txt" 2>/dev/null)
            [ -n "$msg" ] && reason="Codex credential check failed: $msg"
          else
            f="$RUNNER_TEMP/claude-execution-output.json"
            if [ -f "$f" ]; then
              msg=$(jq -r 'if type=="array" then .[] else . end
                           | select(.type? == "result")
                           | (.result // .error // empty)' "$f" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)
              [ -n "$msg" ] && reason="Claude token check failed: $msg"
            fi
            fix="mint a fresh token (claude setup-token) and re-run the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard"
          fi
          echo "::error::$reason - $fix."
          curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
            --data-urlencode "job=seo-token-check" \
            --data-urlencode "fail=$reason - $fix" \
            "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true

      # Pipeline staleness: compare this repo's installed pack version stamp
      # against the backend's current one. Stale is not broken - the report
      # tells the owner an update is waiting; re-running the setup command
      # applies it. Repos installed before version stamps skip silently. A
      # non-200/404 response (401, 5xx, timeout) means the project key itself
      # is rejected, not that pipeline_version is unsupported - that must be
      # loud, not folded into the same silent skip.
      - name: Pipeline update check
        if: always()
        env:
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          [ -f .dispatchseo/pipeline-version ] || { echo "No version stamp (pre-stamp install) - skipping."; exit 0; }
          installed=$(tr -d '[:space:]' < .dispatchseo/pipeline-version)
          code=$(curl -s -o /tmp/mode.json -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 30 \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
            "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/project-mode")
          if [ "$code" = "404" ]; then
            echo "Backend has no pipeline_version yet - skipping."
            exit 0
          elif [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
            echo "::error::project-mode returned HTTP $code - the project key looks rejected by the backend. Re-run the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard to mint a fresh key."
            curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
              --data-urlencode "job=seo-token-check" \
              --data-urlencode "fail=project key rejected by backend (HTTP $code) - re-run the setup command" \
              "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
            exit 1
          fi
          current=$(jq -r '.pipeline_version // empty' /tmp/mode.json)
          if [ -z "$current" ]; then echo "Backend has no pipeline_version yet - skipping."; exit 0; fi
          if [ "$installed" = "$current" ]; then
            echo "Pipeline up to date ($installed)."
            curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
              --data-urlencode "job=seo-pipeline-version" --data-urlencode "ok=1" \
              "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
          else
            echo "::warning::Pipeline update available (installed $installed, current $current). Re-run the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard to apply it."
            curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
              --data-urlencode "job=seo-pipeline-version" \
              --data-urlencode "fail=pipeline update available (installed $installed, current $current) - re-run the setup command to apply" \
              "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
          fi

name: SEO tool validation

# The functional reviewer for autonomously-built tool PRs. A tool PR may only
# auto-merge if this workflow has exercised the LIVE page (real production
# build, real browser) and proven the widget works. On pass it labels the PR
# `tool-validated`; the auto-merge gate requires that label for any PR that
# carries `seo-tool`. On fail it labels `tool-validation-failed` and comments
# the concrete failures so the next builder run (or the owner) can fix them.
#
# Scope: runs ONLY on same-repo PRs labeled seo-tool (the tool builder's PRs).
# Guide PRs never get the seo-tool label and are never gated by this.
#
# Two triggers for the same validation:
# - pull_request: the normal path. BUT tool PRs are opened by the builder
#   with the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN, and since GitHub's 2026-06-11 change
#   those runs are created parked in "action_required" (awaiting manual
#   approval, with no repo-level opt-out) - left alone the PR stalls forever.
# - workflow_dispatch (pr_number input): the escape hatch. Dispatch events
#   created with GITHUB_TOKEN always execute (documented exception), so
#   seo-auto-merge's self-heal dispatches this workflow for any verdict-less
#   tool PR. Both paths converge on the resolve step below, which re-verifies
#   the same-repo + seo-tool gates from live PR state.

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      pr_number:
        description: "Open seo-tool PR number to validate"
        required: true

concurrency:
  group: seo-tool-validate-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || inputs.pr_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  validate:
    # pull_request mode: same-repo PRs only (fork PRs get no secrets anyway)
    # + must be a tool PR. Dispatch mode passes here and is gated by the
    # resolve step instead (its event payload has no PR fields to check).
    if: >
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository &&
       contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'seo-tool'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    # SECURITY: this job builds and RUNS the PR's (LLM-authored) code, so it
    # must never hold a token that can write to the repo. Labels/comments only;
    # the squash-merge lives in the separate `merge` job below, which never
    # checks out or executes PR code.
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
      issues: write # gh label create
    steps:
      # Authoritative gate for BOTH trigger modes: read the PR's live state
      # and refuse anything that is not an open, same-repo, seo-tool PR. Also
      # resolves the head SHA the job checks out, so a dispatched run
      # validates exactly the PR head (not the default branch the dispatch
      # technically runs against).
      - name: Resolve and gate the PR
        id: pr
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number || inputs.pr_number }}
        run: |
          case "$PR_NUMBER" in
            ''|*[!0-9]*) echo "::error::pr_number must be a plain PR number."; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          info=$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
            --json state,isCrossRepository,labels,headRefOid \
            --jq '{state, cross: .isCrossRepository, labels: [.labels[].name], sha: .headRefOid}')
          echo "$info"
          if [ "$(echo "$info" | jq -r .state)" != "OPEN" ] \
             || [ "$(echo "$info" | jq -r .cross)" != "false" ] \
             || ! echo "$info" | jq -e '.labels | index("seo-tool")' >/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::PR #$PR_NUMBER is not an open same-repo seo-tool PR - refusing to validate."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "sha=$(echo "$info" | jq -r .sha)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # The resolved PR head, so both trigger modes exercise the same code.
          ref: ${{ steps.pr.outputs.sha }}
          # Don't leave a git credential on disk for the PR's build scripts to
          # read - this job's steps talk to GitHub only via the env tokens on
          # the specific steps that need them.
          persist-credentials: false

      # Which coding agent validates, plus the fail-fast on a broken credential
      # that used to be a Claude-only preflight here. Both agents get the same
      # plain-language error rather than dying minutes in on a cryptic
      # validation failure - the 2026-07-17 dogfood install burned four runs on
      # exactly that.
      #
      # This job holds an AGENT credential and no project secrets, which is the
      # posture the security note above describes. Worth stating plainly,
      # because it is a real trade and not an oversight: the job executes the
      # PR's LLM-authored code, so whichever agent credential is present is
      # exfiltratable by that code. That was already true of the Claude token;
      # an OpenAI key is the same exposure with a more direct blast radius,
      # being metered money rather than a subscription. Accepted for the same
      # reason as before - these PRs come from this project's own builder on the
      # same repo, never a fork - and it is why the merge job stays separate
      # with no checkout.
      #
      # UNLIKE every other workflow, this one does NOT ask the backend which
      # agent to use. Asking means holding SEO_MCP_API_KEY, and the one thing
      # this job must never do is acquire a reason to hold the project key. A
      # secret is only visible to the step that names it, so the leak would not
      # be direct - but the invariant is worth more than the consistency.
      #
      # The SEO_AGENT repo VARIABLE is the primary answer. Variables (unlike
      # secrets) are readable without holding anything sensitive, and the
      # backend best-effort writes this one on every agent switch and install,
      # so this workflow can agree with the dashboard without asking it.
      # Inference from secret presence remains the fallback for repos whose
      # backend predates the variable - but on its own it was NOT just
      # cosmetic: switching Claude -> Codex leaves the old Claude secret
      # behind (the switch is deliberately a single column write), the
      # tie-break below then picks Claude, and if the owner switched because
      # the Claude subscription lapsed, validation goes red, the
      # tool-validated label never lands, and every tool PR on the project
      # strands unmerged.
      - name: Resolve the coding agent
        id: agent
        env:
          CLAUDE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
          AGENT_VAR: ${{ vars.SEO_AGENT }}
        run: |
          case "$AGENT_VAR" in
            claude|codex) agent="$AGENT_VAR" ;;
            *) if [ -n "$OPENAI_API_KEY" ] && [ -z "$CLAUDE_TOKEN" ]; then agent=codex; else agent=claude; fi ;;
          esac
          case "$agent" in
            claude)
              if [ -z "$CLAUDE_TOKEN" ]; then
                echo "::error::This project validates with Claude Code, but the CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN secret is missing or empty on this repo. Rerun the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard (it mints and VERIFIES a fresh token), or set one by hand: run 'claude setup-token', then pipe the token into 'gh secret set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN' without any whitespace."
                exit 1
              fi
              case "$CLAUDE_TOKEN" in
                sk-ant-oat*) : ;;
                *)
                  echo "::error::CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN does not look like a Claude Code OAuth token (expected it to start with sk-ant-oat). It was probably line-wrapped or the wrong text was pasted when it was saved. Rerun the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard to mint and verify a replacement."
                  exit 1 ;;
              esac ;;
            codex)
              if [ -z "$OPENAI_API_KEY" ]; then
                echo "::error::This project validates with Codex, but the OPENAI_API_KEY secret is missing or empty on this repo. Add it with 'gh secret set OPENAI_API_KEY', or rerun the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard."
                exit 1
              fi
              case "$OPENAI_API_KEY" in
                sk-*) : ;;
                *)
                  echo "::error::OPENAI_API_KEY does not look like an OpenAI key (expected it to start with sk-). It was probably line-wrapped or the wrong text was pasted when it was saved. Create a fresh key at platform.openai.com/api-keys and set it again."
                  exit 1 ;;
              esac ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::The dashboard reported an unknown agent '$agent'. This repo's workflows are older than that setting - re-run the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard to update them."
              exit 1 ;;
          esac
          echo "agent=$agent" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Validating with: $agent"

      # Deliberately NOT an INSTALL-ADAPT step any more. This used to say "if
      # this repo has a packageManager field, DELETE the version input below" -
      # a conditional edit left to whoever ran the install, with a fatal
      # failure mode when it was missed: pnpm/action-setup hard-errors if a
      # version input sits alongside a packageManager pin, so the builder died
      # right here on every run, 13 seconds in, BEFORE reaching the step that
      # reports failures to the dashboard. It shipped that way and broke every
      # installed repo carrying a pin (2026-07-30). The two cases are now two
      # mutually-exclusive steps resolved at RUN time: there is nothing to
      # adapt, so there is nothing to forget. Do not reintroduce a `version:`
      # input on an unconditional step - scripts/pipeline-pack-lint.mjs fails
      # the build if the fatal shape comes back.
      - name: Read this repo's pnpm pin
        id: pnpm_pin
        run: |
          pinned=0
          if [ -f package.json ] && node -e 'process.exit(require("./package.json").packageManager ? 0 : 1)' 2>/dev/null; then
            pinned=1
          fi
          echo "pinned=$pinned" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "packageManager pin in package.json: $pinned"

      # Pinned -> action-setup reads the exact version out of the field.
      # Passing a version input as well is precisely what hard-errors.
      - name: Set up pnpm (version from the repo's packageManager pin)
        if: steps.pnpm_pin.outputs.pinned == '1'
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4

      # No pin -> action-setup has to be told. pnpm 11 matches the Node 22
      # pinned below; a repo whose lockfile was written by an older major
      # should add a packageManager field rather than edit this, which
      # routes it to the exact path above.
      - name: Set up pnpm (no packageManager pin in this repo)
        if: steps.pnpm_pin.outputs.pinned == '0'
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 11

      - name: Set up Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: pnpm

      - name: Install deps
        run: |
          pnpm install --frozen-lockfile || {
            s=$?
            echo "::error::pnpm install failed (exit $s). Frequent causes: (1) ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS - pnpm 11 hard-fails dependencies with unanswered build scripts (strictDepBuilds is on by default): answer each one in pnpm-workspace.yaml (allowBuilds: dep: true/false, plus an onlyBuiltDependencies list for older pnpm) and commit. (2) pnpm/lockfile version mismatch - align the workflow's pnpm with the version that wrote pnpm-lock.yaml (package.json packageManager field). Reproduce locally with a fresh 'pnpm install --frozen-lockfile'."
            exit $s
          }

      - name: Production build
        run: pnpm build
        env:
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL: "https://placeholder.supabase.co"
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY: "placeholder-anon-key"
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL: "http://localhost:3000"

      - name: Start server and wait for it
        run: |
          nohup pnpm start >/tmp/next-server.log 2>&1 &
          for i in $(seq 1 30); do
            code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:3000/ || true)
            [ "$code" = "200" ] && echo "server up" && exit 0
            sleep 2
          done
          echo "server failed to start"; cat /tmp/next-server.log; exit 1
        env:
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL: "https://placeholder.supabase.co"
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY: "placeholder-anon-key"
          NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL: "http://localhost:3000"

      - name: Install Playwright browser for the MCP
        run: npx -y playwright install --with-deps chromium

      # Codex's twin of mcp-validate.json. Written here rather than shipped as a
      # file because this job's MCP surface is one stdio server with no secrets
      # in it - there is nothing to personalize per project, so a file would be
      # a second thing to keep in sync for no benefit.
      - name: Write Codex's MCP config
        if: steps.agent.outputs.agent == 'codex'
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/codex-home"
          cat > "$RUNNER_TEMP/codex-home/config.toml" <<'TOML'
          [mcp_servers.playwright]
          command = "npx"
          args = ["-y", "@playwright/mcp@latest", "--headless", "--isolated"]
          # Nobody is here to approve a tool call on a scheduled runner, and
          # without this every call comes back "user cancelled MCP tool call".
          default_tools_approval_mode = "approve"

          [sandbox_workspace_write]
          # The validator drives a real browser against localhost:3000.
          network_access = true
          TOML

      - name: Validate the tool live
        if: steps.agent.outputs.agent == 'claude'
        id: claude
        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
        with:
          claude_code_oauth_token: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # Tool PRs are opened and pushed by the builder workflow, so the
          # triggering actor is github-actions[bot]; without this the action
          # refuses to start ("non-human actor") and the PR never gets a
          # verdict. Same-repo + seo-tool label gates above still apply.
          allowed_bots: "github-actions"
          # Full transcript in the step log - post-hoc debuggability.
          show_full_output: true
          prompt: "You are the functional validator for an autonomously-built {{SITE_NAME}} tool PR. 1) Find the tool under review: run `git diff origin/main...HEAD --name-only` and read the diff of the tools registry (its path is listed in .dispatchseo/conventions.md) to get the NEW tool's slug (the entry added in this PR). 2) Work out the tool's PUBLIC path - never assume /tools/<slug>: take it from the route/page files the PR added, the registry entry's own path field, or the Tools section of .dispatchseo/conventions.md, and cross-check it against the sitemap. (Sites whose /tools route belongs to a logged-in app publish elsewhere, e.g. /free-tools/<slug>; a login redirect or 404 here means you have the wrong path, not a broken tool - re-derive it before judging.) Using the playwright MCP, open http://localhost:3000<path> and validate: the page returns 200 and renders the landing funnel (hero h1, the interactive widget, FAQ section); every primary widget interaction works (fill each input with realistic values, click every action button, verify output actually updates, test the copy action); edge cases do not break it (empty input, nonsense input - the widget must never throw); zero console errors during the whole session (check browser console messages). 3) Verdict: if EVERYTHING passes, run `gh pr edit <pr-number> --add-label tool-validated --remove-label tool-validation-failed || gh pr edit <pr-number> --add-label tool-validated` and post a short PR comment via `gh pr comment` summarizing what you exercised. If ANYTHING fails, run `gh pr edit <pr-number> --add-label tool-validation-failed --remove-label tool-validated || gh pr edit <pr-number> --add-label tool-validation-failed` (removing tool-validated matters: a stale pass from an earlier commit must not authorize a merge) and comment the concrete failures (what you did, what happened, console output). Create missing labels with `gh label create` if needed. The PR number is in the PR_NUMBER environment variable. Never modify code in this run - you are a reviewer only."
          claude_args: |
            --mcp-config ./.github/mcp-validate.json
            --permission-mode bypassPermissions
            --max-turns 140
        env:
          CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number || inputs.pr_number }}

      # The Codex twin. Same prompt, byte-for-byte - a verdict must not depend
      # on which agent reached it.
      #
      # No turn budget: Codex has no --max-turns equivalent (OpenAI closed the
      # request for one as not-planned), so this job's timeout-minutes is the
      # only ceiling. That is a weaker bound than the 140 above, and the honest
      # place to note it is here.
      - name: Validate the tool live (Codex)
        if: steps.agent.outputs.agent == 'codex'
        id: codex
        uses: openai/codex-action@v1
        with:
          openai-api-key: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
          # Same rule as the Claude twin's allowed_bots above: this workflow is
          # reached by a pull_request opened by github-actions[bot], or by
          # seo-auto-merge's GITHUB_TOKEN dispatch - a bot actor either way.
          # codex-action's actor gate rejects EVERY bot by default (a bot 404s
          # the collaborator-permission lookup), so without this line Codex
          # tool validation never runs at all and tool PRs strand unvalidated.
          # Every trigger that can reach this step already required repo write
          # access, so allowing all actors adds nothing an attacker can use.
          allow-users: "*"
          model: ${{ vars.SEO_CODEX_MODEL || 'gpt-5' }}
          codex-home: ${{ runner.temp }}/codex-home
          sandbox: workspace-write
          safety-strategy: drop-sudo
          output-file: ${{ runner.temp }}/codex-out.txt
          prompt: "ENVIRONMENT RULE (read first, it overrides habit): you have no apply_patch tool here - only the shell, and you are running UNATTENDED, so there is nobody to answer a question. Write every file with a SINGLE-QUOTED heredoc (cat > path <<'DSEOF' ... DSEOF) or with python3 reading the content from stdin. The quoted delimiter is the whole point: bash expands NOTHING inside it, so the backticks and $ in MDX and TSX survive verbatim. NEVER use an unquoted heredoc, printf or echo to write file content - an unquoted heredoc is what expands backticks and corrupts the file. Pick a delimiter that cannot appear in the content. Verify every write with ls -l and head before moving on, and never let a filename come from an unset shell variable. If you ever find yourself about to ask for approval or a go/no-go, do not: pick the safest option that still completes the task, do it, and say what you chose in the final report. A run that stops to ask a question builds nothing and is a failed run. You are the functional validator for an autonomously-built {{SITE_NAME}} tool PR. 1) Find the tool under review: run `git diff origin/main...HEAD --name-only` and read the diff of the tools registry (its path is listed in .dispatchseo/conventions.md) to get the NEW tool's slug (the entry added in this PR). 2) Work out the tool's PUBLIC path - never assume /tools/<slug>: take it from the route/page files the PR added, the registry entry's own path field, or the Tools section of .dispatchseo/conventions.md, and cross-check it against the sitemap. (Sites whose /tools route belongs to a logged-in app publish elsewhere, e.g. /free-tools/<slug>; a login redirect or 404 here means you have the wrong path, not a broken tool - re-derive it before judging.) Using the playwright MCP, open http://localhost:3000<path> and validate: the page returns 200 and renders the landing funnel (hero h1, the interactive widget, FAQ section); every primary widget interaction works (fill each input with realistic values, click every action button, verify output actually updates, test the copy action); edge cases do not break it (empty input, nonsense input - the widget must never throw); zero console errors during the whole session (check browser console messages). 3) Verdict: if EVERYTHING passes, run `gh pr edit <pr-number> --add-label tool-validated --remove-label tool-validation-failed || gh pr edit <pr-number> --add-label tool-validated` and post a short PR comment via `gh pr comment` summarizing what you exercised. If ANYTHING fails, run `gh pr edit <pr-number> --add-label tool-validation-failed --remove-label tool-validated || gh pr edit <pr-number> --add-label tool-validation-failed` (removing tool-validated matters: a stale pass from an earlier commit must not authorize a merge) and comment the concrete failures (what you did, what happened, console output). Create missing labels with `gh label create` if needed. The PR number is in the PR_NUMBER environment variable. Never modify code in this run - you are a reviewer only."
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number || inputs.pr_number }}

      # NO report step here, on purpose: this job builds and RUNS the PR's
      # (LLM-authored) code, so it must hold no secrets at all - not even the
      # project MCP key. Outcome reporting lives in the merge job below,
      # which runs on a fresh runner with no checkout and no untrusted code.

  # The hands-off publish for tools: a PASS verdict from the live validation
  # above IS the merge authorization (the tool was built in prod mode and
  # exercised in a real browser - a stronger gate than any preview check).
  # FAIL or no verdict leaves the PR open for the owner.
  #
  # SECURITY: this is a separate job on a fresh runner precisely so the
  # contents:write token never coexists with the PR's executed code (the
  # validate job above builds and runs the branch). No checkout here - it only
  # reads labels and merges via gh.
  merge:
    needs: validate
    # Dispatch mode passes here by design: the validate job's resolve step
    # already enforced the same-repo + seo-tool gates, and this job re-reads
    # the labels via gh before acting anyway. always() so a FAILED validate
    # still reaches the report step below instead of silently skipping this
    # job - a red validation must land on the dashboard banner.
    if: >
      always() &&
      (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      (github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository &&
       contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'seo-tool')))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: write # squash-merge + branch delete
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      # Phone the validation outcome home from THIS job - never from the
      # validate job, which executes the PR's (LLM-authored) code and must
      # hold no secrets. Failures land on the DispatchSEO dashboard banner +
      # alert email (same rails as the crons); successes clear any earlier
      # red banner row. A skipped validate (non-tool PR) reports nothing.
      - name: Report validation outcome to the dashboard
        if: needs.validate.result == 'success' || needs.validate.result == 'failure'
        env:
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          VALIDATE_RESULT: ${{ needs.validate.result }}
        run: |
          if [ "$VALIDATE_RESULT" = "success" ]; then
            curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
              --data-urlencode "job=seo-tool-validate" --data-urlencode "ok=1" \
              "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
          else
            curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
              --data-urlencode "job=seo-tool-validate" \
              --data-urlencode "fail=validation workflow failed - $RUN_URL" \
              "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
          fi

      - name: Merge on PASS verdict
        if: needs.validate.result == 'success'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number || inputs.pr_number }}
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          # Publish-mode gate: same rule as seo-auto-merge - when the owner
          # turned auto_merge off (semi mode or a custom toggle), a PASS still
          # labels the PR but the merge waits for the dashboard's Merge click.
          code=$(curl -s -o /tmp/mode.json -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 30 \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
            {{BACKEND_URL}}/api/project-mode) || code=unreachable
          if [ "$code" = "200" ] && [ "$(jq -r '.automations.auto_merge' /tmp/mode.json)" = "false" ]; then
            echo "auto_merge is off on the dashboard - leaving the validated PR for the owner."
            exit 0
          elif [ "$code" = "unreachable" ] || [ "$code" = "000" ] || [ "$code" = "502" ] || [ "$code" = "503" ] || [ "$code" = "504" ]; then
            # Local-backend self-host: a GitHub-hosted runner cannot reach a
            # localhost dashboard to read auto_merge. install.ts keeps this
            # workflow ENABLED on local backends, so don't crash - the tool is
            # already built and browser-validated; leave the labeled PR for the
            # dashboard / in-stack builder to merge (matches seo-daily.yml).
            echo "Backend unreachable (local self-host?) - leaving the validated PR for the dashboard to merge."
            exit 0
          elif [ "$code" != "200" ] && [ "$code" != "404" ]; then
            echo "::error::project-mode endpoint returned HTTP $code"; exit 1
          fi

          labels=$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json labels -q '.labels[].name')
          # Both conditions: tool-validated present AND no failure flag. A stale
          # tool-validated from an earlier commit must never merge a newer,
          # failing state of the branch.
          if echo "$labels" | grep -qx "tool-validated" && ! echo "$labels" | grep -qx "tool-validation-failed"; then
            echo "Validated - squash-merging PR #$PR_NUMBER."
            gh pr merge "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --squash --delete-branch || {
              gh pr comment "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --body "Validation passed but auto-merge failed (likely a conflict with main). Manual merge needed."
              # A merge failure used to die invisibly in this job - report it
              # so the banner + email say the PR is waiting on a human.
              curl -sG --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
                --data-urlencode "job=seo-tool-validate" \
                --data-urlencode "fail=validation passed but auto-merge failed (likely a conflict with main) - PR left open for manual merge" \
                "{{BACKEND_URL}}/api/cron/deploy-check" || true
              exit 1
            }
            # The squash push above is made with GITHUB_TOKEN, which never
            # triggers push-event workflows - dispatch IndexNow explicitly so
            # the new tool URL gets pinged (no blog slugs; the ping reads the
            # live sitemap).
            gh workflow run indexnow.yml --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
              || echo "IndexNow dispatch failed - the sitemap still covers the URL on the next crawl."
          else
            echo "No tool-validated label - leaving the PR open for review."
          fi

name: SEO tool builder

# Builds the oldest APPROVED tool suggestion into a PR through the seo-manager
# skill's /seo-build-tool pipeline (claude-md-generator template -> live SERP
# gate -> theme discovery -> execution plan + value bar -> build -> humanizer
# -> PR labeled seo + seo-tool).
#
# Tools are approve-idea-first: nothing builds until the user greenlights the
# concept on the dashboard. Three triggers:
#   1. repository_dispatch "seo-tool-approved" - fired both the moment a tool
#      suggestion is approved AND by the backend's scheduler when the weekly
#      cadence comes due with something approved waiting (api/cron/seo-dispatch).
#      This is the real schedule now.
#   2. Weekly cron (Wednesday 19:42 UTC) - a DEAD-MAN'S SWITCH for a backend
#      that cannot dispatch at all. It was three crons (05:42, 12:42, 19:42)
#      purely to self-heal a trigger GitHub might drop; the backend re-fires
#      until a run reports back, so the other two were paying GitHub's
#      one-minute-minimum to discover there was nothing to do.
#   3. workflow_dispatch - manual runs.
# If the queue has no approved tools, the run exits cleanly - and the backend
# will not dispatch at all in that case, so the runner never starts.
#
# Merging: tool PRs are NOT merged by this workflow. The seo-tool-validate
# workflow smoke-tests the built tool live and labels it tool-validated; the
# auto-merge gate only merges tool PRs carrying that label.

on:
  repository_dispatch:
    types: [seo-tool-approved]
  schedule:
    - cron: "42 19 * * 3" # Wednesdays 19:42 UTC - dead-man's switch only, see above
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: seo-tool-build
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # The agent commits below. Pin an identity that maps to a real GitHub
      # account - Vercel refuses to deploy commits from unknown author emails,
      # and an unconfigured runner leaves the agent to improvise one.
      - name: Pin git identity to github-actions[bot]
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

      - name: Skip if a tool PR is already open or tool builds are toggled off
        id: guard
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
        run: |
          open=$(gh pr list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --label seo-tool --state open --json number --jq 'length')
          if [ "$open" != "0" ]; then
            echo "A tool PR is already open - skipping. The suggestion stays approved; the weekly sweep will pick it up once the open PR lands."
          fi
          # Automation-flag gate: the DispatchSEO dashboard can pause tool
          # builds (auto_build_tools off). 404 = backend without the endpoint
          # yet -> build as before; other failures are loud.
          if [ "$open" = "0" ]; then
            code=$(curl -s -o /tmp/mode.json -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 30 \
              -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
              {{BACKEND_URL}}/api/project-mode) || code=unreachable
            if [ "$code" = "200" ] && [ "$(jq -r '.automations.auto_build_tools' /tmp/mode.json)" = "false" ]; then
              echo "Tool builds are toggled off on the dashboard - skipping. The suggestion stays approved."
              open=paused
            elif [ "$code" = "unreachable" ] || [ "$code" = "000" ] || [ "$code" = "502" ] || [ "$code" = "503" ] || [ "$code" = "504" ]; then
              # Self-hosted backends reboot (kernel updates, docker restarts).
              # Unreachable is a delay, not a failure - the later scheduled
              # attempt and the in-stack builder both cover this window.
              echo "Backend unreachable right now (rebooting?) - deferring to the next scheduled attempt."
              open=defer
            elif [ "$code" != "200" ] && [ "$code" != "404" ]; then
              echo "::error::project-mode endpoint returned HTTP $code"; exit 1
            fi
          fi
          # Already-ran-today gate, for the dead-man's cron: it must not redo
          # work an earlier dispatch already did the same day. Reuses the
          # project-mode fetch above (same tolerant rule: anything but a clean
          # "true" reads as "not run yet").
          # SCHEDULE-only. This exists so the fallback does not redo the
          # dispatched run's work; it was never meant to gate an ON-DEMAND run.
          # Without the event_name test, an owner approving a tool after that
          # day's sweep had the build silently skipped - every step no-op'd, the
          # final step still reported ok=1, and the next chance was seven days
          # later (2026-07-27).
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "schedule" ] && [ "$open" = "0" ] && [ "$code" = "200" ] && [ "$(jq -r '.ran_today."seo-tools" // false' /tmp/mode.json 2>/dev/null)" = "true" ]; then
            echo "Today's tool sweep already ran - skipping this attempt."
            open=skip
          fi
          # Empty-queue gate. The backend never dispatches with nothing
          # approved, so this is for the dead-man's cron: without it, a weekly
          # fallback on a project with an empty tool queue starts a full
          # coding-agent session purely to have the agent exit clean.
          # Absent field (older backend) or any non-200 reads as "work is
          # waiting", so this can only ever cost a run, never suppress one.
          if [ "$open" = "0" ] && [ "$code" = "200" ] && [ "$(jq -r '.approved_waiting.tool // true' /tmp/mode.json 2>/dev/null)" = "false" ]; then
            echo "No approved tool suggestions are waiting - nothing to build."
            open=skip
          fi
          echo "open=$open" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # Which coding agent builds this project - resolved at RUN time from the
      # dashboard, never baked in at install time.
      #
      # Same rule as the pnpm pin below, for the same reason: a decision left to
      # whoever ran the install is a decision someone eventually forgets, and the
      # failure mode here is a builder that runs the wrong agent every night.
      # Asking the backend means switching agent on the dashboard takes effect on
      # the next scheduled run with nothing to edit in this repo.
      #
      # The fallback matters as much as the happy path: a repo installed against
      # a backend that predates the `agent` field gets no value here, and must
      # keep behaving exactly as it did - which is Claude, because Claude was the
      # only option that ever existed before the field.
      - name: Resolve the coding agent
        id: agent
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0'
        env:
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
          CLAUDE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          agent=""
          code=$(curl -s -o /tmp/agent.json -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 30 \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
            {{BACKEND_URL}}/api/project-mode) || code=unreachable
          [ "$code" = "200" ] && agent=$(jq -r '.agent // empty' /tmp/agent.json 2>/dev/null)
          if [ -z "$agent" ] || [ "$agent" = "null" ]; then
            # No answer from the backend. Infer from which secret exists, and
            # tie-break to claude - see the note above.
            if [ -n "$OPENAI_API_KEY" ] && [ -z "$CLAUDE_TOKEN" ]; then agent=codex; else agent=claude; fi
            echo "Backend did not name an agent (HTTP $code) - inferred '$agent' from the secrets on this repo."
          fi
          # Fail here, in plain language, rather than letting the agent's own
          # action die minutes in on a cryptic validation error. The 2026-07-17
          # dogfood install burned four runs on exactly that.
          case "$agent" in
            claude)
              if [ -z "$CLAUDE_TOKEN" ]; then
                echo "::error::This project builds with Claude Code, but the CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN secret is missing or empty on this repo. Rerun the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard (it mints and VERIFIES a fresh token), or set one by hand: run 'claude setup-token', then pipe the token into 'gh secret set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN' without any whitespace."
                exit 1
              fi
              case "$CLAUDE_TOKEN" in
                sk-ant-oat*) : ;;
                *)
                  echo "::error::CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN does not look like a Claude Code OAuth token (expected it to start with sk-ant-oat). It was probably line-wrapped or the wrong text was pasted when it was saved. Rerun the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard to mint and verify a replacement."
                  exit 1 ;;
              esac ;;
            codex)
              if [ -z "$OPENAI_API_KEY" ]; then
                echo "::error::This project builds with Codex, but the OPENAI_API_KEY secret is missing or empty on this repo. Add it with 'gh secret set OPENAI_API_KEY', or rerun the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard."
                exit 1
              fi
              case "$OPENAI_API_KEY" in
                sk-*) : ;;
                *)
                  echo "::error::OPENAI_API_KEY does not look like an OpenAI key (expected it to start with sk-). It was probably line-wrapped or the wrong text was pasted when it was saved. Create a fresh key at platform.openai.com/api-keys and set it again."
                  exit 1 ;;
              esac ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::The dashboard reported an unknown agent '$agent'. This repo's workflows are older than that setting - re-run the setup command from your DispatchSEO dashboard to update them."
              exit 1 ;;
          esac
          echo "agent=$agent" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Building with: $agent"

      # Fail loudly if the seo-manager MCP is unreachable. Without this, a
      # stale URL in mcp-ci.json makes Claude see an empty toolset and "exit
      # cleanly" - a green run that built nothing (2026-07-14 domain-move bug).
      - name: Preflight - seo-manager MCP reachable
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0'
        env:
          SEO_MCP_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.SEO_MCP_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          url=$(node -e "console.log(require('./.github/mcp-ci.json').mcpServers['seo-manager'].url)")
          code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 30 -X POST "$url" \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $SEO_MCP_API_KEY" \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
            -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":0,"method":"tools/list"}')
          if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
            echo "::error::seo-manager MCP at $url returned HTTP $code - fix the URL in .github/mcp-ci.json or the SEO_MCP_API_KEY secret"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "seo-manager MCP OK ($url)"

      # Deliberately NOT an INSTALL-ADAPT step any more. This used to say "if
      # this repo has a packageManager field, DELETE the version input below" -
      # a conditional edit left to whoever ran the install, with a fatal
      # failure mode when it was missed: pnpm/action-setup hard-errors if a
      # version input sits alongside a packageManager pin, so the builder died
      # right here on every run, 13 seconds in, BEFORE reaching the step that
      # reports failures to the dashboard. It shipped that way and broke every
      # installed repo carrying a pin (2026-07-30). The two cases are now two
      # mutually-exclusive steps resolved at RUN time: there is nothing to
      # adapt, so there is nothing to forget. Do not reintroduce a `version:`
      # input on an unconditional step - scripts/pipeline-pack-lint.mjs fails
      # the build if the fatal shape comes back.
      - name: Read this repo's pnpm pin
        id: pnpm_pin
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0'
        run: |
          pinned=0
          if [ -f package.json ] && node -e 'process.exit(require("./package.json").packageManager ? 0 : 1)' 2>/dev/null; then
            pinned=1
          fi
          echo "pinned=$pinned" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "packageManager pin in package.json: $pinned"

      # Pinned -> action-setup reads the exact version out of the field.
      # Passing a version input as well is precisely what hard-errors.
      - name: Set up pnpm (version from the repo's packageManager pin)
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0' && steps.pnpm_pin.outputs.pinned == '1'
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4

      # No pin -> action-setup has to be told. pnpm 11 matches the Node 22
      # pinned below; a repo whose lockfile was written by an older major
      # should add a packageManager field rather than edit this, which
      # routes it to the exact path above.
      - name: Set up pnpm (no packageManager pin in this repo)
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0' && steps.pnpm_pin.outputs.pinned == '0'
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 11

      - name: Set up Node
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0'
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: pnpm

      - name: Install deps (so the skill's `pnpm build` verify step works)
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0'
        run: |
          pnpm install --frozen-lockfile || {
            s=$?
            echo "::error::pnpm install failed (exit $s). Frequent causes: (1) ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS - pnpm 11 hard-fails dependencies with unanswered build scripts (strictDepBuilds is on by default): answer each one in pnpm-workspace.yaml (allowBuilds: dep: true/false, plus an onlyBuiltDependencies list for older pnpm) and commit. (2) pnpm/lockfile version mismatch - align the workflow's pnpm with the version that wrote pnpm-lock.yaml (package.json packageManager field). Reproduce locally with a fresh 'pnpm install --frozen-lockfile'."
            exit $s
          }

      # Codex reads its MCP servers from a config.toml inside its own home
      # directory. Two things here are easy to get wrong and both are silent:
      #
      # 1. The action does NOT honour an inbound CODEX_HOME env var - it takes a
      #    `codex-home` INPUT and sets the env itself. Writing a config to a
      #    hand-rolled $CODEX_HOME and hoping is a no-op, and the failure looks
      #    like an agent with no tools rather than an error.
      # 2. `sandbox: workspace-write` blocks network by default, which kills MCP
      #    over HTTP. The network_access line below is what makes the sandboxed
      #    posture usable at all.
      - name: Write Codex's MCP config
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0' && steps.agent.outputs.agent == 'codex'
        env:
          DATAFORSEO_LOGIN: ${{ secrets.DATAFORSEO_LOGIN }}
          DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/codex-home"
          cp .github/mcp-codex.toml "$RUNNER_TEMP/codex-home/config.toml"
          cat >> "$RUNNER_TEMP/codex-home/config.toml" <<'TOML'

          [sandbox_workspace_write]
          network_access = true
          TOML
          # Render the DataForSEO credential tokens. Codex's TOML `env` map is
          # LITERAL - it does not expand ${VAR} the way Claude expands its JSON
          # config - so left alone the dataforseo server would authenticate as
          # the literal string "${DATAFORSEO_LOGIN}" and every keyword call
          # would 401 mid-build. python3 rather than sed so no credential
          # character can break the substitution; values are TOML-escaped. A
          # truncated config (free-mode project, no dataforseo section) makes
          # this a no-op.
          python3 - "$RUNNER_TEMP/codex-home/config.toml" <<'PY'
          import os, sys
          path = sys.argv[1]
          text = open(path).read()
          for token, var in (("${DATAFORSEO_LOGIN}", "DATAFORSEO_LOGIN"),
                             ("${DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD}", "DATAFORSEO_PASSWORD")):
              val = os.environ.get(var, "").replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"')
              text = text.replace(token, val)
          open(path, "w").write(text)
          PY
          echo "Codex home prepared. Servers configured:"
          grep -E '^\[mcp_servers\.' "$RUNNER_TEMP/codex-home/config.toml"

      - name: Run the SEO tool builder
        if: steps.guard.outputs.open == '0' && steps.agent.outputs.agent == 'claude'
        id: claude
        # Never fail the job at this step: the classify step below reads the
        # outcome and decides what the run MEANS (deferral vs failure), which
        # it can only do if it is reachable.
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
        with:
          # Cloud fires this as the DispatchSEO GitHub App (a Bot actor), and the App also authored the workflow commits, so scheduled runs are bot-actored too. Every trigger here needs repo write access, so allowing bots is safe; without this claude-code-action aborts with "non-human actor".
          allowed_bots: "*"
          claude_code_oauth_token: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          # Standard workflow token as input so the action skips the Claude
          # GitHub App exchange (same pattern as seo-daily.yml).
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # Full transcript in the step log - post-hoc debuggability.
          show_full_output: true
          prompt: "FIRST call the seo-manager MCP tool get_instructions with workflow build-tool, then follow the returned markdown exactly - it is the current playbook and overrides any cached knowledge of this pipeline. Also read .dispatchseo/conventions.md for this repo's site facts (registry wiring, reference implementation, theme tokens).
